newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SCHOLTEN KEEPS AJAX ON COURSE FOR LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHOLTEN KEEPS AJAX ON COURSE FOR LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Ajax stayed on course for a place in the European Cup quarter-finals with a deserved but hard-won 1-0 victory over a weakened Rangers side in a Champions' League group A match on Wednesday.

The only goal of a fiercely-contested game came after 39 minutes when midfielder Arnold Scholten lashed home a low, powerful 25-metre drive which flew past the outstretched right arm of Rangers' Dutch goalkeeper Theo Snelders.
The defeat was Rangers' fourth in succession, confirming their elimination with two matches to play. Ajax now have nine points from their four matches.

Rangers, missing four players through suspension and without another six injured players, were forced to give a first team debut to 19-year-old defender Scott Wilson and play 20-year-old defender Greg Shields, who had made only two previous appearances.

But the youngsters gave a good account of themselves against the Dutch champions who, despite controlling the match for long periods, could never relax and had a fortunate let-off after 59 minutes when Joerg Albertz skied a close-range shot when it looked easier to score.
The only black mark for Ajax was a second-half booking for Marcio Santos which rules him out of their next match against Auxerre of France on November 20.
